# Step 1 — Package setup & data loading

```{r}

# 1. Load libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(readr)
library(readxl)
library(sf)
library(tigris)
library(tidycensus)
library(spdep)
library(viridis)
library(patchwork)
library(lubridate)
library(janitor)
# library(jsonlite)

options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)   # cache tigris downloads locally
census_api_key("d43934f52489c25471f4f6e0942464d34a9052a8",install = T, overwrite = T)

# 2. Dataset A — Dog Licensing
dogs_raw <- read_csv("data/Dog_Licensing.csv") |> clean_names()
glimpse(dogs_raw)

# 3. Dataset B — Dog Bites
bites_raw <- read_csv("data/Dog_Bite.csv") |> clean_names()
glimpse(bites_raw)

# 4. Dataset C — Dog Runs
# runs_raw <- read_json("https://data.cityofnewyork.us/api/views/hxx3-bwgv/rows.json?accessType=DOWNLOAD")
# glimpse(runs_raw)

# 5. Dataset E — ZCTA boundaries via tigris
# nyc_zips <- c(Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, Bronx, Staten Island)
  # tigris will pull all NY ZCTAs; we filter to NYC after

zcta_all <- zctas(cb = TRUE, year = 2020)
# Filter to NYC ZCTAs after joining with licensing data

# 6. Dataset D — ACS median income via tidycensus
income_raw <- get_acs(
  geography = "zcta",
  variables = "B19013_001",   # median household income
  year = 2022,
  survey = "acs5"
)
glimpse(income_raw)

```

# PHASE 2: Data Checking & Cleaning

## A: Dog Licensing

```{r}
# A: Dog Licensing

# 1. Check overall missingness
cat("=== Dataset A: Missingness ===\n")
dogs_raw |> summarise(across(everything(), ~mean(is.na(.)))) |> 
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "column", values_to = "pct_missing") |>
  arrange(desc(pct_missing)) |> print(n = 17)

# 2. Check extract_year range
cat("\n=== Extract year distribution ===\n")
dogs_raw |> count(extract_year) |> print()

# 3. Check zipcode validity — NYC zips start with 100xx-104xx or 110xx-114xx
cat("\n=== Invalid zipcodes ===\n")
dogs_raw |> 
  filter(!str_detect(as.character(zipcode), "^(100|101|102|103|104|110|111|112|113|114)")) |>
  count(zipcode) |> arrange(desc(n)) |> print

# 4. Duplicate check
cat("\n=== Duplicate rows ===\n")
cat("Total duplicates:", sum(duplicated(dogs_raw)), "\n")

# 5. Gender distribution
cat("\n=== Gender values ===\n")
dogs_raw |> count(animalgender) |> print()


```

## B: Dog Bites

```{r}
# 1. Missingness
cat("\n=== Dataset B: Missingness ===\n")
bites_raw |> summarise(across(everything(), ~mean(is.na(.)))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "column", values_to = "pct_missing") |>
  arrange(desc(pct_missing)) |> print()

# 2. Date range
cat("\n=== Bite date range ===\n")
cat("Min:", format(min(bites_raw$dateofbite, na.rm=TRUE)), "\n")
cat("Max:", format(max(bites_raw$dateofbite, na.rm=TRUE)), "\n")

# 3. Species check — should all be DOG
cat("\n=== Species values ===\n")
bites_raw |> count(species) |> print()

# 4. Borough values
cat("\n=== Borough values ===\n")
bites_raw |> count(borough) |> arrange(desc(n)) |> print()

# 5. Zipcode issues in B
cat("\n=== Bite zipcode issues ===\n")
bites_raw |> 
  filter(!str_detect(zipcode, "^(100|101|102|103|104|110|111|112|113|114)") | is.na(zipcode)) |>
  count(zipcode) |> arrange(desc(n)) |> print(n = 20)
```

## C: Dog Runs — load from NYC Open Data JSON

```{r}
# The raw JSON from that URL is NYC Socrata format, not GeoJSON
# Use the GeoJSON endpoint instead:
dog_runs <- st_read("https://data.cityofnewyork.us/api/geospatial/hxx3-bwgv?method=export&type=GeoJSON")
cat("\n=== Dog runs CRS ===\n")
st_crs(dog_runs)
cat("\n=== Dog runs columns ===\n")
glimpse(dog_runs)
cat("\n=== Dog runs count ===\n")
nrow(dog_runs)
```
### As Step below, which found can not transter json file into sf, so change format of this dataset.

```{r}
# Check dog runs CSV
dog_runs_raw <- read_csv("data/Dog_Runs.csv") |>
  clean_names()

glimpse(dog_runs_raw)
names(dog_runs_raw)

# Dataset C — parse WKT geometry from the_geom column
dog_runs_sf <- dog_runs_raw |>
  filter(!is.na(the_geom)) |>                        # all 91 rows have geometry
  st_as_sf(wkt = "the_geom", crs = 4326) |>          # parse WKT, assign WGS84
  mutate(borough_full = case_when(
    borough == "M" ~ "Manhattan",
    borough == "B" ~ "Brooklyn",
    borough == "Q" ~ "Queens",
    borough == "X" ~ "Bronx",
    borough == "R" ~ "Staten Island",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  ))

# Sanity checks
cat("Dog runs loaded:", nrow(dog_runs_sf), "\n")
cat("CRS:", st_crs(dog_runs_sf)$input, "\n")
cat("Borough distribution:\n")
dog_runs_sf |> st_drop_geometry() |> count(borough_full)

# Visual check
plot(st_geometry(zcta_nyc), col = "grey90", border = "white")
plot(st_geometry(dog_runs_sf), col = "steelblue", add = TRUE)
```


# D: Income — filter to NYC ZCTAs only
```{r}
# Use 2022 ACS (best match for 2016-2023 dog data window)
income_raw <- get_acs(
  geography = "zcta",
  variables = "B19013_001",
  year = 2022,
  survey = "acs5"
)
head(income_raw)
str(income_raw)

# NYC zipcodes list (all 5 boroughs)
nyc_zip_list <- dogs_raw |> 
  filter(str_detect(as.character(zipcode), "^(100|101|102|103|104|110|111|112|113|114)")) |>
  pull(zipcode) |> unique() |> as.character()

income_nyc <- income_raw |>
  filter(GEOID %in% nyc_zip_list) |>
  rename(zip = GEOID, median_income = estimate) |>
  select(zip, median_income, moe)

cat("\n=== Income: NYC ZCTAs retained ===\n")
nrow(income_nyc)
cat("\n=== Income: NA estimates ===\n")
sum(is.na(income_nyc$median_income))
```

## E: ZCTA boundaries — filter to NYC
```{r}
zcta_nyc <- zctas(cb = TRUE, year = 2020) |>
  filter(ZCTA5CE20 %in% nyc_zip_list)

cat("\n=== ZCTA NYC polygons ===\n")
nrow(zcta_nyc)
plot(st_geometry(zcta_nyc))  # quick sanity check — should look like NYC
```

```{r}
zcta_all <- zctas(cb = TRUE, year = 2020)

nyc_bbox <- st_bbox(c(xmin = -74.26, ymin = 40.49,
                       xmax = -73.70, ymax = 40.92),
                    crs = st_crs(4326)) |> st_as_sfc()

zcta_nyc <- zcta_all |>
  st_transform(4326) |>
  filter(st_intersects(geometry, nyc_bbox, sparse = FALSE)[,1])

nyc_zip_list <- zcta_nyc$ZCTA5CE20
cat("NYC ZCTAs from tigris:", length(nyc_zip_list), "\n")
```
